When I came into this office, I told you I would be honest about what we could do and what we couldn’t. Looking back, I’m proud of what we’ve done together — the jobs we’ve created, the families who now have health coverage, the progress we’ve made on equality — but I’m just as aware of what remains unfinished. Democracy isn’t a spectator sport. It depends on all of us showing up, listening to people we disagree with, and being willing to compromise when the moment demands it. I’ve seen the best of this country in ordinary places: in classrooms, in hospital corridors, in town halls where neighbors argued and then shook hands. That is what gives me hope. My message to you is simple: don’t give up on each other, and don’t give up on the idea that we can do better.
